pr_title: Fix `mouse_mode` returning the wrong value in the web platform
pr_comments:
This does not fully fix the issue in my testing. Opening the MRP (Window Management Demo) in a custom build that includes this PR, with custom Web export templates set to web builds that include this PR, pressing Run in Browser, and pressing F3 (which should set the mouse mode to captured) *without first clicking in the browser viewport* sets the mouse mode to captured while still showing the mouse (which is game-breaking).

(It should fail to set the mode to captured if there hasn't been a click inside the browser viewport before it.)

issue_context.title: [Web] `Input.mouse_mode` returns wrong value
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.4.dev4.official [36e6207bb]
- Reproducible in v4.4.dev7.official [46c8f8c5c]
- Not reproducible in v4.4.dev3.official [f4af8201b]

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev4 - CachyOS Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu, 19 Dec 2024 21:23:18 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER (nvidia; 565.77) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9700K CPU @ 3.60GHz (8 threads), Web export tested under Firefox 133.0.3 (64-bit)

### Issue description

In **web exports** `Input.mouse_mode` sometimes returns `MouseMode.MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE` despite setting it to `MouseMode.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED` and behaving like it is captured.

### Steps to reproduce

1. open "Window Management" from [official demo projects](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/misc/window_management)
2. add web export, run the project in browser (Remote Debug)
3. click on the MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED button or press <kbd>F3</kbd>
4. Extra hints should appear below all the MouseModes buttons:

> ESC: Deactivate MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED
> W, S: Move forward, backward
> A, D: Strafe left, right

At least they do in v4.4.dev3 but not in v4.4.dev4 anymore since the condition `Input.get_mouse_mode() == Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED` evaluates to `false`.

There is a case, when this evaluates to `true`:
1. run the project in browser anew or refresh the page
2. click somewhere inside the window, on the cube for example
3. press <kbd>F3</kbd>, <kbd>F1</kbd>, <kbd>F3</kbd> in that order.
4. Notice extra hints being shown also in `v4.4.dev4` or `v4.4.dev7`
 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

"Window Management" official demo project (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/misc/window_management)
comments:
> Anyone on [@godotengine/web](https://github.com/orgs/godotengine/teams/web) could answer me if setting the mouse mode in the web is not immediate?

Hiding it is immediate, capturing/releasing it is async due to the underlying API being async -> https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestPointerLock

Just a question to help get this fixed for web is a more simplified MRP needed because I would be willing to create one. Because as of 4.4.dev4 grabbing the mouse for input is completely broken for me. Thank you all for your help. I hope @YeldhamDev 's PR get merged soon and that it fixes the issue.

[web-mouse-capture-part-2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18604433/web-mouse-capture-part-2.zip)

I would like to re-open this issue. I have discovered an edge case that likely happens often. When the mouse is captured browsers tend to tell the user that they can press escape to free there mouse. If we capture the users mouse and then they press escape we can not again capture it with the current behavior. Even though the engine knows that the mouse has been released. To capture the mouse again after the user has pressed escape we must first tell the engine to release the mouse and then capture it again. So that they engine executes the correct sequence.



## Tested versions:

- Reproducible in Godot 4.4.beta2

## Steps to reproduce:

1. Extract MRP
2. Open MRP in Godot 4.4.beta2
3. Ensure exports are managed for Godot 4.4.beta2
4. Run the MRP in the browser.
5. Capture the mouse using the button provided.
6. Press the escape key "esc".
7. Observe that your mouse is released and visible.
8. Attempt to capture the mouse using the button provided that says "Capture Mouse".
9. Observe this does not work.
10. Press the button that says "Capture Mouse After Release".
11. Observe this works.

Alternatively for step 10. You can also press space bar or press the "Release Mouse" button. and then you can press the "Capture Mouse" button and it will work.

review_comments:
I think this `mouse_mode = p_mode` line can be removed, and the early return if `p_mode == mouse_mode` should be moved inside if `#ifndef WEB_ENABLED` block, and `Input::get_mouse_mode` should return `get_mouse_mode_func()` if `WEB_ENABLED` is defined (i.e. a more complete revert of the PR that caused the issue).

This fixes the issue in my game.

I would also move the comment to the `#else` block. You can add me as coauthor of the PR if you like.
The problem is that those changes would make the return of `get_mouse_mode()` be the override value instead of the one set by the user.
I created https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101849 which goes more in depth about how `mouse_mode` is updated when the platform sets it async.
